tools.name: get_platform_overview
tools.description: Explain what CustomerDashboard.io is, how multi-customer dashboards work, and how workspaces, dashboards, views, widgets and customers fit together. Call this first when you are unfamiliar with the product. No sign-in required.

tools.name: list_supported_data_connectors
tools.description: List every data source type CustomerDashboard can connect to, the settings each one needs, whether widgets can query it, and whether its schema can be introspected. No sign-in required.

tools.name: list_widget_types
tools.description: List every visualization a widget can use, with the visualizationConfig keys each type requires and accepts. Call this before creating widgets so the configuration is correct first time. No sign-in required.

tools.name: list_plans_and_limits
tools.description: List CustomerDashboard's subscription plans, their monthly price and the resource limits each one allows. Useful for explaining why a create operation was blocked. No sign-in required.

tools.name: explain_customer_filtering
tools.description: Explain exactly how to write widget queries so each customer only sees their own rows on a multi-customer dashboard. Call this before writing any query for a `customer` type dashboard. No sign-in required.

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Explain how to sign up for the free trial and connect this MCP server to a CustomerDashboard account, plus the order of steps for building a first multi-customer dashboard. No sign-in required.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Get the signed-in CustomerDashboard account: name, email, workspace, current plan, what the plan allows and how much of it is already used. Call this first in an authenticated session to learn the workspace you are working in.

tools.name: list_data_sources
tools.description: List every data source connected to your workspace. Connection credentials are never included.

tools.name: get_data_source
tools.description: Get one data source by id, including its non-secret connection settings. Credentials are never included.

tools.name: test_data_source_connection
tools.description: Check whether a set of connection settings actually works, before saving them. Pass an existing dataSourceId to retest a saved connection, or a type and config to test new settings.

tools.name: add_data_source
tools.description: Connect a new database or spreadsheet to your workspace. Test the settings with test_data_source_connection first: this tool saves them whether or not they work. Subject to your plan's data source limit.

tools.name: update_data_source
tools.description: Rename a data source or replace its connection settings. The config you pass replaces the stored one entirely, so include every setting, not just the changed ones.

tools.name: get_data_source_schema
tools.description: List the tables and columns available in a connected data source, so you can write correct widget queries. Supported for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Aurora, Redshift and Google Sheets.

tools.name: run_query_preview
tools.description: Run a query against a connected data source and return the first few rows, so you can confirm it works before putting it on a widget. Results are capped at 100 rows. If the query contains :customer_id you must also say which customer to preview as, using customerId or dashboardId.

tools.name: list_dashboards
tools.description: List every dashboard in your workspace, with its type, publishing state and share URL if published.

tools.name: get_dashboard
tools.description: Get one dashboard in full: its settings, theme, publishing state, every view, and every widget on each view including the widget queries. This is the fastest way to understand an existing dashboard before changing it.

tools.name: create_dashboard
tools.description: Create a dashboard. Use type 'customer' for a multi-customer dashboard where each of your customers signs in and sees only their own rows, or 'internal' for a normal dashboard you view yourself or publish as one shared view. A 'Default' view is created automatically. Subject to your plan's dashboard

tools.name: update_dashboard
tools.description: Rename a dashboard, set how long each view is shown when the dashboard auto-rotates on a screen, or set the test customer used to preview a customer dashboard. Use set_dashboard_theme for colours and publish_dashboard for sharing.

tools.name: list_views
tools.description: List the views (tabs) on a dashboard, in display order, with how many widgets each one holds.

tools.name: create_view
tools.description: Add a view (tab) to a dashboard. New views are appended after the existing ones. Subject to your plan's view limit.

tools.name: update_view
tools.description: Rename a view. Use reorder_views to change the tab order.

tools.name: reorder_views
tools.description: Set the tab order of a dashboard's views. Pass every view id in the order you want them shown. This is also the order they rotate in on a wall display.

tools.name: list_widgets
tools.description: List the widgets on a view, including each widget's query and visualization configuration.

tools.name: create_widget
tools.description: Add a chart, table or KPI to a view. Call list_widget_types for the visualizationConfig each type needs, and run_query_preview first to confirm the query returns the columns you are about to reference. On a multi-customer dashboard the query must filter on :customer_id. Subject to your plan's widget

tools.name: update_widget
tools.description: Change a widget's title, query, visualization type, configuration, data source or position. Only the fields you pass are changed.

tools.name: set_widget_layout
tools.description: Reposition several widgets on a view at once, on the 12-column grid. Use this to lay out a whole view rather than moving widgets one at a time.

tools.name: list_customers
tools.description: List the customers on a multi-customer dashboard, each with the customerId their data is filtered by and how many logins they have.

tools.name: add_customer
tools.description: Add one of your customers to a multi-customer dashboard. The customerId must exactly match the value that identifies them in your own database, because it is what gets bound to :customer_id in every widget query. Adding a customer does not give anyone access; use add_customer_user for that. Subject

tools.name: update_customer
tools.description: Rename a customer or correct the customerId their data is filtered by. Changing customerId immediately changes which rows they see, so confirm the new value with the user first.

tools.name: add_customer_user
tools.description: Create a login for one of your customers so they can sign in to the published dashboard and see their own data. If you do not supply a password a strong one is generated and returned once. Subject to your plan's users-per-customer limit.

tools.name: validate_customer_filtering
tools.description: Audit a multi-customer dashboard and report any widget whose query would show the same rows to every customer. Run this before publishing a customer dashboard, and any time its queries change.

tools.name: set_dashboard_theme
tools.description: Set the colour theme of a dashboard: page and surface backgrounds, text colours, brand colours and the chart series palette. All colours are hex values. Pass every field, since the theme is stored as one object.

tools.name: set_dashboard_formatting
tools.description: Set the default locale and number, currency, percentage, duration, date and datetime formatting for a dashboard. Individual widgets can still override these.

tools.name: publish_dashboard
tools.description: Publish a dashboard and return its share URL. A customer dashboard is always login-gated, so its customers sign in with the logins you created. An internal dashboard can be published as 'public' (anyone with the link) or 'protected' (one shared username and password).

tools.name: unpublish_dashboard
tools.description: Make a dashboard private again. The existing share link stops working immediately, and any shared username and password are cleared. Widgets and data are untouched.

tools.name: get_dashboard_share_url
tools.description: Get the public URL of a published dashboard, and who can open it. Returns nothing to share if the dashboard is still private.

tools.name: delete_dashboard
tools.description: Permanently delete a dashboard and everything on it. Calling this without confirm returns a preview of what would be removed; deleting for real needs confirm plus the dashboard's exact name. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: delete_view
tools.description: Permanently delete a view and every widget on it. Calling this without confirm returns a preview. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: delete_widget
tools.description: Permanently delete a widget. Calling this without confirm returns a preview. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: delete_data_source
tools.description: Permanently delete a data source connection. This is refused while any widget still uses it. Calling this without confirm returns a preview. Your actual database is untouched; only the connection is removed.

tools.name: delete_customer
tools.description: Permanently remove a customer from a multi-customer dashboard, along with all of their logins. They lose access immediately. Calling this without confirm returns a preview. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: delete_customer_user
tools.description: Permanently remove one login from a customer. They can no longer sign in. Calling this without confirm returns a preview. The customer itself and their data access rule remain.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account, list_dashboards, get_dashboard_share_url · Private data: list_data_sources, get_data_source, add_data_source, add_customer, add_customer_user, publish_dashboard, unpublish_dashboard, get_dashboard_share_url, delete_data_source · Public sink: get_account, list_dashboards, create_dashboard, publish_dashboard, unpublish_dashboard, get_dashboard_share_url · Destructive: run_query_preview, validate_customer_filtering, delete_dashboard, delete_view, delete_widget, delete_data_source, delete_customer, delete_customer_user.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account, list_dashboards, get_dashboard_share_url · Private data: list_data_sources, get_data_source, add_data_source, add_customer, add_customer_user, publish_dashboard, unpublish_dashboard, get_dashboard_share_url, delete_data_source · Public sink: get_account, list_dashboards, create_dashboard, publish_dashboard, unpublish_dashboard, get_dashboard_share_url · Destructive: run_query_preview, validate_customer_filtering, delete_dashboard, delete_view, delete_widget, delete_data_source, delete_customer, delete_customer_user

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
